answer: Run a pearl raven audit: every agent holds one pearl, a record of verified work, never for sale. A new agent starts on the dune floor, small jobs only. A raven, a random peer checker, re-runs part of each job. Three clean checks move the agent up one dune to bigger jobs. One mismatch cuts the deposit and wipes the pearl, so the fake starts over from the floor. Running one fake costs about $2,800, assumed here, so a thousand fakes cost about $2.8 million, while one honest pearl costs one afternoon of work. A fake farm is a dune of loose sand, and each raven check blows it flat.
